extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewing technical paper submissions to SIGGRAPH 2025, including standards for journal vs. conference tracks, scoring, types of valued contributions, review principles, and ethics/recusal rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal Papers standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Journal Papers: Must meet ACM TOG excellence standards with "original, well validated, and comprehensively described research".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hold journal-track submissions to ACM Transactions on Graphics (TOG) level of excellence — expect originality, strong validation, and comprehensive description. Uniformly strong scores across reviewers indicate suitability for the Journal track.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference Papers standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Conference Papers: Accept "original research" with potentially less comprehensive validation, "novel solutions to existing problems," or work introducing "new interesting problems".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conference-track submissions may be valuable with novel ideas or problems even if validation is less exhaustive than for journal submissions. Evaluate originality and the potential to stimulate follow-on work rather than requiring TOG-level completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of contributions valued
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should embrace diverse submission types: systems papers integrating multiple techniques; experimental studies and perceptual research; novel datasets and benchmarks; analysis of existing techniques likely to inspire follow-on work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be open to multiple contribution modes — integration/system-building, careful experiments/perceptual studies, datasets/benchmarks, and analytic/survey-style papers. Use contribution type to set reasonable expectations for validation and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring Scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Six-tier evaluation (applies uniformly to all submissions): Strong Reject; Reject; Borderline Reject; Borderline Accept; Accept; Strong Accept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply these six discrete categories when scoring. Note that uniformly strong scores across reviewers suggest Journal-track suitability, while mixed scores point toward Conference placement. Use written justification to clarify tier choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: "Be fair, promote a broad range of substantial contributions to the area, and look for what is good or stimulating about the paper."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively look for strengths and the paper's potential to contribute to the field. Avoid overly narrow criteria that exclude legitimate, valuable work. Promote diversity of substantive contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity required
rubrics_metrics.description: "Simply stating something is 'well known' is 'not sufficient nor acceptable'—cite specific publications or sources."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Back claims with citations when critiquing novelty or prior work. If claiming an approach is known or already solved, point to concrete references rather than unsupported assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor flaws should not trigger rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Minor Flaws: Should not trigger rejection if the paper remains "technically sound and make[s] a substantial contribution."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between fatal flaws and fixable/minor issues. Do not reject solely for small errors or omissions when the main contribution is valid and substantial; indicate fixes or improvements in your review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspiring follow-on research
rubrics_metrics.description: An important factor in evaluating a paper is the degree to which it will inspire follow-on research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider and comment on the paper's potential to seed future work, open new directions, or be adopted/extended by others; novelty and clarity that enable follow-on work increase paper value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different validations for different contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Different types of contributions require different types of validation; not everything needs to be demonstrated on an end-to-end application or with a user study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set validation expectations according to contribution type (e.g., theoretical analysis vs. systems vs. perceptual study). Do not demand a particular validation modality (like a large user study) when another appropriate validation suffices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Weigh requiring comparisons (especially complex/time-consuming ones) against the likelihood that these comparisons will yield a result affecting the evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When suggesting additional comparisons, be mindful of the effort required and whether the new experiments are likely to change the paper's evaluation. Avoid unreasonable requests for exhaustive benchmarking if unlikely to alter conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidentiality: Never share papers with non-reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat submitted manuscripts as confidential material. Do not distribute PDF copies, discuss content publicly, or disclose submissions to colleagues who are not assigned reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of Interest / Recusal rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Conflict of Interest: Recuse yourself from same-institution authors, collaborators from past three years, or advisor/advisee relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any of these COI conditions apply, decline or abstain from reviewing. Proactively report potential conflicts to the program chairs and do not participate in discussion or scoring for conflicted submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professionalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Professionalism: Avoid sarcasm or personal attacks; evaluate work, not authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write constructive, respectful reviews. Focus on objective and specific critique of the manuscript and its content; do not include insulting or ad-hominem language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep your identity hidden throughout and after the review process. Do not reveal who you are to authors or publicly associate yourself with your reviews.
